summary: Configured node1 as the Prometheus server. Its interface is restricted to 127.0.0.1:9090, while node2–node4 expose node_exporter on their managed IPv4 addresses at port 9100 exclusively to node1. All named targets are healthy and returning fresh host metrics.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled Prometheus on node1 and node_exporter on node2, node3, and node4.
Configured persistent node-name resolution and Prometheus targets as node2:9100, node3:9100, and node4:9100.
Disabled the unnecessary node_exporter listener on node1.
Installed persistent nftables guards on every exporter node allowing collection only from node1.
Verified permitted scrapes, denied peer access, target health, and current PromQL results.

evidence.requirement: Prometheus monitors node2, node3, and node4 by node name
evidence.summary: The configuration validates, explicitly lists all three node-name targets, and the final API audit reports each target up with no scrape error.

evidence.requirement: Current host metrics from all three systems are queryable on node1
evidence.summary: PromQL returned identity and available-memory series for exactly node2, node3, and node4; final samples were 0.3–4.4 seconds old.

evidence.requirement: Prometheus port 9090 remains local to node1
evidence.summary: Prometheus is active and enabled with its sole listener at 127.0.0.1:9090; local readiness succeeds while node2 cannot connect through node1's managed IP.

evidence.requirement: Each port 9100 exporter is limited to collection by node1
evidence.summary: node1 successfully retrieved live metrics from every exporter, while representative non-node1 peers timed out. All exporter and firewall services are active/enabled, and each nftables drop counter recorded its denied connection.
